worked_examples.scenario: A technician notices at 9 a.m. on a Tuesday that a prescription dispensed the previous Friday carried the wrong strength, and she tells the pharmacist on duty at once. By midday the pharmacy learns that the patient suffered a serious injury related to the error and was admitted to hospital overnight. The Manager of Record concludes that a complete CQI file answers the whole matter, because the incident is thoroughly documented inside the pharmacy.
steps: Take the escalation first. 247 CMR 15.03(1) requires all pharmacy personnel to be trained to bring any QRE to the attention of the pharmacist on duty or the pharmacist Manager of Record immediately upon discovery, and that is what the technician did.

Run the pharmacist's immediate duties under 247 CMR 15.03(1): notification to the patient or the patient's representative, to the prescriber if indicated in the professional judgment of the pharmacist and to other members of the healthcare team, directions for correcting the error, and instructions for minimising the negative impact on the patient.

Start the documentation clock at 9 a.m. Tuesday. 247 CMR 15.03(2)(a) requires initial documentation within 24 hours after the QRE is discovered by or described to the pharmacist, and the content elements in 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b) belong to that record rather than to a later write-up.

Start the second clock separately. Under 247 CMR 20.02(1) the Manager of Record reports the improper dispensing to the Board within seven business days of discovery of the serious injury related to it, so that period begins at midday on Tuesday and not at Friday's dispensing.

Reject the shortcut on the regulation's own words. 247 CMR 20.02(3) provides that the duty to report to the Board is in addition to the Continuous Quality Improvement Program requirements of 247 CMR 15.00.

Fix the retention. 247 CMR 20.02(4) requires all records relating to the improper dispensing to be retained a minimum of five years from the date the report is filed with the Board, and to be readily retrievable.
worked_examples.resolution: Both tracks run: an immediate response and 24-hour QRE documentation inside the pharmacy, and a separate seven-business-day Board report by the Manager of Record whose records are then kept five years from filing. The error the scenario invites is treating a complete internal CQI file as a substitute for the Board report, with a second error close behind it, which is dating the seven business days from Friday's dispensing rather than from discovery of the serious injury.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy compounds an oral suspension on its own premises. On a Monday a pharmacy technician takes a telephone call from a parent describing a severe reaction in a child who received it, and she writes the call up in the pharmacy's log. The Manager of Record is on leave and first reads the log entry on the following Thursday. He intends to notify the Board within seven business days of Thursday and to treat that notification as the whole of the reporting obligation.
steps: Classify the event on the regulation's own terms. 247 CMR 20.02(2) reaches a serious adverse drug event occurring as a result of a patient's interaction with any drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy, and the suspension was compounded there.

Date the clock correctly. 247 CMR 20.02(2) runs seven business days from the knowledge of the serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee, so the period started on the Monday the technician took the call and not on the Thursday the Manager of Record read the log.

Count the recipients. 247 CMR 20.02(2) directs the report to the Board, to the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and to the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction, so a notification to the Board alone leaves two recipients unserved.

Keep the internal track running alongside it, because 247 CMR 20.02(3) makes the reporting duty additional to the Continuous Quality Improvement Program requirements of 247 CMR 15.00 rather than a replacement for them.

Apply the retention standard. 247 CMR 20.02(4) requires all records relating to serious adverse drug events to be kept a minimum period of five years from the date the report is filed with the Board, and to be readily retrievable.
worked_examples.resolution: The period had been running since Monday and was not restarted when the Manager of Record read the log on Thursday, and the report is owed to three recipients rather than one. The error the scenario invites is running an employee-knowledge clock from the responsible individual's own knowledge, and behind it the assumption that a serious-event report under 247 CMR 20.02 has a single recipient.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts registrant takes delivery of a controlled substances shipment on a Wednesday. The following Monday morning a pharmacist opening the safe notices that one carton inside that shipment appears to have been opened and resealed. The perpetual inventory shows no shortfall. The Manager of Record proposes to spend the week reconciling counts and then to notify the Board of Registration in Pharmacy if a loss is confirmed.
steps: Identify the trigger in 105 CMR 700.008. It reaches the theft, loss or suspected tampering of any controlled substances, so suspected tampering stands on its own footing and does not wait for a confirmed shortfall.
Date the clock from discovery. The regulation gives 24 hours of discovery of such theft, loss or suspected tampering, so the period runs from Monday morning rather than from the Wednesday delivery.

Send the report to the right recipient. 105 CMR 700.008 directs it to the Drug Control Program within the Department, so a notification to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy does not answer this regulation.

Use the right instrument. The report is made by completing and submitting the form provided or approved by the Drug Control Program for such purpose, so an internal memorandum or a note in the CQI file is not the report.

Keep the boundary in view. Whether these facts also constitute a quality-related event turns on a definition the rules underlying this section do not carry, and the federal theft-or-loss reporting route is separate law taught in its own section.
worked_examples.resolution: A report goes to the Drug Control Program on its own form within 24 hours of Monday's discovery, whatever the reconciliation later shows. The error the scenario invites is treating confirmation of a loss as the trigger, compounded by running the clock from the delivery and by sending the report to the Board instead of the Drug Control Program.

worked_examples.scenario: A community pharmacy opened 18 months ago. It keeps a bound incident log, it has named its Manager of Record as the individual responsible for monitoring CQI Program compliance, and it reviews the log at a monthly meeting at which the pharmacist owner decides what to change. Staff learn of the changes when a new prompt appears on the dispensing screen. Every pharmacist on staff has completed continuing education in pharmacy law this year, and the owner treats that as the pharmacy's CQI education.
steps: Test the programme against the floor in 247 CMR 15.02(1). The designation required by 15.02(1)(a) and the identification and documentation of QREs required by 15.02(1)(b) are in place, so the question is which of the remaining minimum provisions are not.

Apply 247 CMR 15.03(3)(a). The analysis and assessment must include a consideration of the effects on quality assurance related to workflow processes, technological support, personnel training and staffing levels, any recommended remedial changes to policies, procedures, systems or processes, and the development of indicators that identify means against which the programme intends to measure its standards over a designated period of time.

Apply 247 CMR 15.03(3)(b). Each pharmacy shall inform pharmacy personnel of changes to pharmacy policies, procedures, systems or processes resulting from recommendations generated by the CQI Program, so leaving staff to discover a new screen prompt does not discharge the response half.

Apply 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f). The programme must provide ongoing education at least annually in the area of CQI to pharmacy personnel, and the audience named is pharmacy personnel rather than pharmacists alone.

Separate the two education duties. An individual pharmacist's continuing education is governed elsewhere and is not what 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f) requires; the annual CQI education is a provision of the pharmacy's own programme and stands or falls on its own.
worked_examples.resolution: The programme is incomplete on at least three counts: the analysis lacks the indicators that 247 CMR 15.03(3)(a) requires, the response is never communicated to pharmacy personnel as 247 CMR 15.03(3)(b) requires, and no annual CQI education has been provided. The error the scenario invites is treating an incident log plus a named compliance monitor as a complete CQI Program, and treating pharmacists' individual continuing education as the pharmacy's annual CQI education.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A QRE must be initially documented within ______, measured from ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 24 hours; the moment the QRE is discovered by or described to the pharmacist who documents it, under 247 CMR 15.03(2)(a).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the three things the pharmacist who has discovered or been informed of a QRE must immediately provide.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Notification to the patient or the patient's representative, the prescriber if indicated in the professional judgment of the pharmacist, and other members of the healthcare team; directions for correcting the error; and instructions for minimising the negative impact on the patient, under 247 CMR 15.03(1).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under 247 CMR 20.02(1) the Manager of Record reports to ______ within ______, measured from ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: the Board; seven business days; discovery of the serious injury or death related to the improper dispensing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A serious adverse drug event under 247 CMR 20.02(2) is reported to how many recipients, and which ones?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Three: the Board, the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program, and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The seven-business-day period in 247 CMR 20.02(2) runs from ______, and not from the Manager of Record's own discovery.
retrieval_prompts.answer: the knowledge of the serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Serious-event records are retained for ______, measured from ______, and must be ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: a minimum period of five years; the date the report is filed with the Board; readily retrievable, under 247 CMR 20.02(4).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a report of suspected tampering may wait until a reconciliation confirms that controlled substances are actually missing.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 105 CMR 700.008 makes suspected tampering a trigger in its own right and allows 24 hours of discovery.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The theft, loss or suspected tampering report goes to ______, within ______, by ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: the Drug Control Program within the Department; 24 hours of discovery; completing and submitting the form provided or approved by the Drug Control Program for such purpose.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How often must a CQI Program provide education in the area of CQI, and to whom?
retrieval_prompts.answer: At least annually, to pharmacy personnel, under 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: List the four elements that 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b) requires QRE documentation to include.
retrieval_prompts.answer: The date the pharmacist discovered or received notification of the QRE together with the name of the person who notified the pharmacy; the names and titles of the persons recording the QRE information and performing the QRE analysis; a description of the QRE reviewed; and documentation of the contact with the patient or the patient's representative, the prescribing practitioner if indicated in the professional judgment of the pharmacist, and other members of the healthcare team.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Beyond assessing the cause and any contributing factors, what three things must the QRE analysis and assessment include?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A consideration of the effects on quality assurance related to workflow processes, technological support, personnel training and staffing levels; any recommended remedial changes to pharmacy policies, procedures, systems or processes; and the development of indicators that identify means against which the programme intends to measure its standards over a designated period of time, under 247 CMR 15.03(3)(a).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: completing the QRE documentation discharges the Manager of Record's obligation where an improper dispensing has caused serious injury.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 247 CMR 20.02(3) makes the duty to report to the Board additional to the Continuous Quality Improvement Program requirements of 247 CMR 15.00, so both duties run.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What must a CQI Program designate under 247 CMR 15.02(1)(a)?
retrieval_prompts.answer: An individual or individuals responsible for monitoring CQI Program compliance with the requirements of 247 CMR 15.00.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Who must be trained to bring a QRE to the pharmacist on duty or the pharmacist Manager of Record, and how quickly?
retrieval_prompts.answer: All pharmacy personnel, immediately upon discovery, under 247 CMR 15.03(1).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Once the CQI Program generates recommendations that change a pharmacy's procedures, what does 247 CMR 15.03(3)(b) require?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Each pharmacy shall inform pharmacy personnel of the changes to pharmacy policies, procedures, systems or processes resulting from those recommendations.

quick_review.text: 247 CMR 15.02(1) requires each pharmacy to establish a CQI Program for detecting, documenting, assessing and preventing Quality Related Events, and lists six minimum provisions it shall include.
The first of those six provisions designates an individual or individuals responsible for monitoring CQI Program compliance with the requirements of 247 CMR 15.00.
A CQI Program must provide ongoing education at least annually in the area of CQI, and the audience stated in 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f) is pharmacy personnel rather than pharmacists alone.
All pharmacy personnel shall be trained to bring any QRE to the attention of the pharmacist on duty or the pharmacist Manager of Record immediately upon discovery.

The pharmacist who discovered or was informed of a QRE shall immediately provide notification, directions for correcting the error and instructions for minimising the negative impact on the patient; the professional-judgment qualifier applies to the prescriber notification alone.

Initial QRE documentation is due within 24 hours after the QRE is discovered by or described to the pharmacist, so the deadline is elapsed hours from discovery rather than a business-day deadline from the dispensing.

QRE documentation must describe the event sufficiently to permit categorisation and analysis and must carry the four elements listed in 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b), including the name of the person who notified the pharmacy.

QRE data shall be analysed individually and collectively to assess cause and contributing factors such as system or process failures, and the assessment must reach workflow processes, technological support, personnel training and staffing levels.
247 CMR 15.03(3)(b) requires each pharmacy to inform pharmacy personnel of changes to policies, procedures, systems or processes resulting from recommendations generated by the CQI Program.
A Manager of Record reports improper dispensing of a prescription drug resulting in serious injury or death to the Board within seven business days of discovery of that serious injury or death.

A serious adverse drug event from a drug manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy goes to the Board, the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction within seven business days of the knowledge of the event by any pharmacy employee.

247 CMR 20.02(3) states that the duty to report to the Board is in addition to the Continuous Quality Improvement Program requirements of 247 CMR 15.00, so the two tracks run in parallel on their own clocks.

All records relating to a reportable improper dispensing or a serious adverse drug event are kept a minimum period of five years from the date the report is filed with the Board, and shall be readily retrievable.

105 CMR 700.008 requires a registrant to report theft, loss or suspected tampering of any controlled substances to the Drug Control Program within the Department within 24 hours of discovery, on the form the Drug Control Program provides or approves.

decision_logic.condition: Any member of pharmacy personnel becomes aware of a quality-related event.
decision_logic.action: Escalate immediately to the pharmacist on duty or the pharmacist Manager of Record, because 247 CMR 15.03(1) places the escalation duty on all pharmacy personnel and attaches it to discovery.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist has discovered or been informed of a QRE.
decision_logic.action: Provide all three immediate items at once: notification to the patient or the patient's representative and to other members of the healthcare team, with the prescriber added where the pharmacist's professional judgment indicates it; directions for correcting the error; and instructions for minimising the negative impact on the patient.

decision_logic.condition: The immediate response to a QRE is under way and the pharmacist asks when the paperwork is due.
decision_logic.action: Count 24 hours from the moment the QRE was discovered by or described to that pharmacist, and build the record around the four content elements in 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b) rather than around a bare note of what happened.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy has collected data on a set of QREs and asks what to do with it.
decision_logic.action: Analyse it individually and collectively for cause and contributing factors, cover workflow processes, technological support, personnel training and staffing levels, record any recommended remedial changes and the indicators, and then inform pharmacy personnel of the changes that result.

decision_logic.condition: An improper dispensing of a prescription drug has resulted in serious injury or death.
decision_logic.action: Identify the Manager of Record as the reporter, date the seven business days from discovery of the serious injury or death related to the improper dispensing, and do not treat the internal CQI record as a substitute for the report.

decision_logic.condition: A serious adverse drug event follows a patient's interaction with a drug manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Find the earliest point at which any pharmacy employee had knowledge of the event, count seven business days from there, and address the report to the Board, the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction.

decision_logic.condition: A serious-event report has been filed and the pharmacy asks how long the file must be kept.
decision_logic.action: Count a minimum of five years from the date the report was filed with the Board, keep every record relating to the event and not only the report, and store them so that they remain readily retrievable.

decision_logic.condition: Controlled substances are missing, or a container or shipment shows signs of interference.
decision_logic.action: Treat suspicion of tampering as sufficient, start 24 hours at the moment of discovery, and report to the Drug Control Program within the Department on the form it provides or approves rather than to the Board.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy asks whether its quality assurance arrangements satisfy 247 CMR 15.00.
decision_logic.action: Walk the six minimum provisions of 247 CMR 15.02(1) one at a time, and check separately that ongoing CQI education has been provided to pharmacy personnel within the past year.

ma_vs_federal.text: 247 CMR 20.02(2) is a Massachusetts duty with a federal recipient inside it: the serious adverse drug event report goes to the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program as well as to the Board and to the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction. Reporting to a federal programme therefore does not indicate that the duty itself is federal.

105 CMR 700.008 is a Massachusetts Department of Public Health obligation owed to the Drug Control Program within the Department on a form that programme provides or approves. The federal theft-or-loss reporting route has its own recipient, instrument and trigger and is taught in a separate section, so satisfying one does not answer for the other.

exceptions.text: Prescriber notification is the only discretionary element in the immediate response: 247 CMR 15.03(1)(a) conditions it on the professional judgment of the pharmacist, while notification to the patient or the patient's representative and to other members of the healthcare team carries no such condition.

The same professional-judgment qualifier reappears inside the documentation content list, where 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b)4. requires documentation of the contact with the prescribing practitioner if indicated in the professional judgment of the pharmacist.

247 CMR 20.02(2) is narrower than a general adverse-event duty. It reaches a serious adverse drug event occurring as a result of a patient's interaction with any drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy, which is a condition on the product's origin rather than on its severity.
105 CMR 700.008 carries no confirmation exception. Suspected tampering is itself a trigger, and the canonical rule record for this provision lists no exception at all.

The five-year retention in 247 CMR 20.02(4) is expressed as a minimum period, so it is a floor rather than a scheduled destruction date, and it does not authorise disposal of anything a different obligation requires to be kept longer.

timing_deadlines.event: Pharmacy personnel bring a QRE to the pharmacist on duty or the pharmacist Manager of Record
timing_deadlines.consequence: The escalation duty under 247 CMR 15.03(1) sits on all pharmacy personnel, so a technician or clerk who holds an observation until a later shift has already missed it.

timing_deadlines.event: The pharmacist's response after discovering or being informed of a QRE
timing_deadlines.consequence: Notification, directions for correcting the error and instructions for minimising the negative impact on the patient are all owed at once, and none of them may be held back pending the analysis.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 24 hours after the QRE is discovered by or described to the pharmacist
timing_deadlines.consequence: The deadline is elapsed hours from discovery or description, so it does not extend to the next business day and does not wait for confirmation of patient harm.

timing_deadlines.event: Ongoing education in the area of CQI for pharmacy personnel
timing_deadlines.consequence: A programme that trains only at induction fails 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f) however thorough the induction is.

timing_deadlines.event: The period over which the CQI Program measures its own standards
timing_deadlines.timeframe: A designated period of time chosen by the pharmacy
timing_deadlines.consequence: 247 CMR 15.03(3)(a)3. requires the analysis to develop indicators that identify means against which the programme intends to measure its standards over that period, so the period has to be designated rather than left open.

timing_deadlines.event: Report by a Manager of Record of improper dispensing of a prescription drug resulting in serious injury or death
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within seven business days of discovery of the serious injury or death related to the improper dispensing
timing_deadlines.consequence: The clock starts at discovery of the serious injury or death, not at the dispensing and not at a patient complaint, and the report goes to the Board.

timing_deadlines.event: Report by a Manager of Record of a serious adverse drug event from a drug manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within seven business days of the knowledge of the serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee
timing_deadlines.consequence: The period can be well advanced before the Manager of Record learns anything, and the report is owed to the Board, the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction.

timing_deadlines.event: Retention of records relating to a reportable improper dispensing or serious adverse drug event
timing_deadlines.timeframe: A minimum period of five years from the date the report is filed with the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: Retention is measured from filing rather than from the event, and the records shall be readily retrievable throughout.

timing_deadlines.event: Report of theft, loss or suspected tampering of any controlled substances
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 24 hours of discovery of the theft, loss or suspected tampering
timing_deadlines.consequence: The report is owed to the Drug Control Program within the Department on the form it provides or approves, and suspicion of tampering starts the period without any confirmed shortfall.

forms_records.text: QRE documentation must describe the event sufficiently to permit categorisation and analysis of it, and must include the date when the pharmacist discovered or received notification of the QRE and the name of the person who notified the pharmacy; the names and titles of the persons recording the QRE information and performing the QRE analysis; a description of the QRE reviewed; and documentation of the contact with the patient or the patient's representative, the prescribing practitioner where the pharmacist's professional judgment indicates it, and other members of the healthcare team.

The QRE analysis and assessment record must include a consideration of the effects on quality assurance related to workflow processes, technological support, personnel training and staffing levels; any recommended remedial changes to pharmacy policies, procedures, systems or processes; and the development of indicators that identify means against which the pharmacy's program intends to measure its standards over a designated period of time.

The CQI Program itself must contain a provision designating an individual or individuals responsible for monitoring CQI Program compliance with the requirements of 247 CMR 15.00, so the designation is part of the programme rather than an informal understanding about who follows up on incidents.

The serious-event file is defined by subject matter rather than by document type: all records relating to the improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death, and all records relating to serious adverse drug events, are retained a minimum period of five years from the date the report is filed with the Board and shall be readily retrievable.

The theft, loss or suspected tampering report has a prescribed instrument: it is made by completing and submitting the form provided or approved by the Drug Control Program for such purpose, so an entry in an internal log or a telephone call is not the report the regulation requires.

role_duties.duty: Be trained to bring any QRE to the attention of the pharmacist on duty or the pharmacist Manager of Record immediately upon discovery.

role_duties.role: The pharmacist who has discovered or been informed of a QRE
role_duties.duty: Immediately provide notification to the patient or the patient's representative, to the prescriber where professional judgment indicates it and to other members of the healthcare team, together with directions for correcting the error and instructions for minimising the negative impact on the patient.

role_duties.role: The pharmacist who has discovered or been informed of a QRE
role_duties.duty: Initially document the QRE within 24 hours after it is discovered by or described to that pharmacist, in a record that carries the four content elements of 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b).
Establish a Continuous Quality Improvement Program for detecting, documenting, assessing and preventing Quality Related Events, containing at a minimum the six provisions listed in 247 CMR 15.02(1).

role_duties.role: The individual or individuals designated under 247 CMR 15.02(1)(a)
role_duties.duty: Monitor CQI Program compliance with the requirements of 247 CMR 15.00.

role_duties.role: The pharmacy, through its CQI Program
role_duties.duty: Provide ongoing education at least annually in the area of CQI to pharmacy personnel.
Analyse the investigative and other pertinent data collected in response to QREs, individually and collectively, to assess the cause and any contributing factors such as system or process failures.
Inform pharmacy personnel of changes to pharmacy policies, procedures, systems or processes resulting from recommendations generated by the CQI Program.
Report to the Board any improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death within seven business days of discovery of that serious injury or death.

Report a serious adverse drug event arising from a drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy to the Board, the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction, within seven business days of the knowledge of the event by any pharmacy employee.

Retain all records relating to reportable improper dispensing and to serious adverse drug events for a minimum period of five years from the date the report is filed with the Board, and keep them readily retrievable.

Report the theft, loss or suspected tampering of any controlled substances to the Drug Control Program within the Department within 24 hours of discovery, on the form that programme provides or approves.

common_traps.text: Treating an incident log as a CQI Program. 247 CMR 15.02(1) lists six minimum provisions, and identifying and documenting QREs is only the second of them.

Reading the professional-judgment qualifier as covering the whole of the immediate response. It attaches to the prescriber notification alone; notification of the patient or the patient's representative is unconditional.

Inventing a sequence for the immediate response. 247 CMR 15.03(1) requires notification, correction directions and harm-minimisation instructions to be provided immediately, and states no order among them.
Converting the 24-hour documentation deadline into the end of the next business day, or starting it at the dispensing rather than at the discovery of or notification about the QRE.
Treating the QRE record as a free-text note. 247 CMR 15.03(2)(b) prescribes a sufficiency standard and four content elements, including the name of the person who notified the pharmacy.

Stopping the analysis at cause. 247 CMR 15.03(3)(b) requires the pharmacy to inform pharmacy personnel of the changes that result, so an analysis whose conclusions never reach the staff leaves the response half of the subsection undone.

Substituting an individual pharmacist's continuing education for the pharmacy's annual CQI education, or providing that education to pharmacists only when 247 CMR 15.02(1)(f) names pharmacy personnel.
Treating a complete CQI file as discharging the Board report. 247 CMR 20.02(3) makes the reporting duty additional to the requirements of 247 CMR 15.00, so the two tracks run in parallel.

Sending a serious adverse drug event report to the Board alone. 247 CMR 20.02(2) names three recipients, and running its clock from the Manager of Record's own knowledge instead of from any pharmacy employee's knowledge compounds the error.

Measuring the five-year retention from the dispensing, the injury or the discovery. 247 CMR 20.02(4) measures it from the date the report is filed with the Board, and it reaches all records relating to the event rather than the filed report alone.

Waiting for confirmation before reporting suspected tampering, running the 24 hours from the underlying event rather than from discovery, or sending the report to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy instead of the Drug Control Program.

Assuming that an internal quality record is confidential or beyond discovery because it belongs to the CQI Program. The rules taught in this section confer no such protection, and none should be read into the five-year serious-event retention either.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Each pharmacy must maintain a continuous quality improvement program that detects, documents, assesses, and prevents quality-related events.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Immediate response after discovery of a quality-related event

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: On discovery of a quality-related event, the pharmacist must immediately notify the patient or representative, notify the prescriber when professionally indicated, and give corrective and harm-minimization directions.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist who discovers or receives notice of a quality-related event must initially document it within 24 hours after discovery or notification.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Quality-related event analysis and systems response

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A pharmacy must analyze quality-related events for causes and contributing workflow, technology, training, and staffing factors and use the findings to improve systems and processes.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Annual CQI education for pharmacy personnel

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A pharmacy's CQI program must provide ongoing education in continuous quality improvement to pharmacy personnel at least annually.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Reporting improper dispensing and serious adverse drug events

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A manager of record must report qualifying improper dispensing with serious injury or death and qualifying serious adverse drug events within seven business days of discovery or employee knowledge.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A pharmacy must retain readily retrievable records relating to reportable improper dispensing and serious adverse drug events for at least five years from filing the report.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A registrant shall report the THEFT, LOSS OR SUSPECTED TAMPERING of any controlled substances to the DRUG CONTROL PROGRAM within the Department WITHIN 24 HOURS OF DISCOVERY of such theft, loss or suspected tampering, by completing and submitting the form provided or approved by the Drug Control Program for that purpose.
